name: Food
facts: Honey never spoils; edible honey has been found in ancient Egyptian tombs.
Bananas are botanically berries, but strawberries are not.
Peanuts are not nuts; they are legumes, like beans and lentils.
Carrots were not always orange; early cultivated carrots were often purple or yellow.
Chillies were brought to India by Portuguese traders in the 16th century.
Apples float in water because about a quarter of their volume is air.
Cashews grow attached to a fruit called the cashew apple.
Tomatoes are fruits, botanically speaking.
Saffron is one of the most expensive spices because each flower yields only three tiny stigmas.
India is the world's largest producer of milk.
Pineapples take around two years to grow.
White chocolate contains no cocoa solids, only cocoa butter, sugar and milk.
Avocados are fruits and are botanically classed as large berries.
Potatoes were the first vegetable grown in space, in 1995.
Ketchup was once sold as a medicine in the United States in the 1830s.
The hottest chilli peppers can be hundreds of times hotter than a jalapeño.
Cucumbers are about 95% water.
Rice is a staple food for more than half the world's population.
Black pepper was once so valuable it was called 'black gold'.
Almonds are seeds of a fruit related to peaches and plums.
Popcorn pops because water inside the kernel turns to steam and bursts the shell.
Turmeric gets its bright yellow colour from a compound called curcumin.
Mangoes are the national fruit of India, Pakistan and the Philippines.
Broccoli, cabbage, cauliflower and kale are all varieties of the same plant species.
Chocolate was drunk as a bitter beverage by the Aztecs and Maya long before it became a sweet treat.
